questions: What is the exact range of values for the elements in the good sequence S?
How should the case be handled when multiple valid sequences have the same score?
Is the modulo value specified anywhere in the problem or should we assume a standard large prime?
What happens when gcd(P,Q) = 1 but either P or Q equals 1 in the definition of f(x)?
Are there any additional constraints on the sequence S elements beyond being positive integers?
Should we consider sequences with repeated elements as distinct when calculating the sum of scores?
Is there a specific order in which the good sequences should be processed or counted?
What is the precise definition of "finitely many good sequences" in terms of the proof mentioned?
answers: Not specified beyond being positive integers satisfying the divisibility/gcd conditions; no explicit upper bound is given beyond what's implied by A_i ≤ 1000.
Each good sequence contributes its own score to the sum regardless of whether other sequences share the same score; no deduplication by score value.
Not an issue; f(x)=P×Q is well-defined whenever P and Q are coprime, including when one of them is 1.
Not specified beyond being positive integers satisfying the stated equations and gcd condition.
Distinctness is by the sequence itself (as a tuple), not by score; different sequences are counted separately even if they'd yield the same score.
Not applicable; the sum is order-independent.
Not detailed beyond what's given; the finiteness guarantee is stated but not elaborated on here.

For a positive rational number x, define f(x) as follows:
Express x as $\dfrac{P}{Q}$ using coprime positive integers P and Q. f(x) is defined as the value P\times Q.
You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_{N-1}) of positive integers of length N-1.
We call a sequence S=(S_1,S_2,\dots,S_N) of positive integers of length N a good sequence if it satisfies all of the following conditions:
- For every integer i with 1\leq i\leq N-1, it holds that f$\left(\dfrac{S_i}{S_{i+1}}\right)$=A_i.
- $\gcd(S_1,S_2,\dots,S_N)=1$.

Output

- All input values are integers.
